### On the current state of Japanese consumer

Japan’s consumer backdrop is improving, supported by a tightening labour market and stronger household purchasing power. Labour demand remains robust as acute labour shortages continue to strengthen workers’ bargaining power. Employment rates have taken another leg higher since March 2026, while the associated wage gains are increasingly feeding through to household incomes. Importantly, wage growth is now running sufficiently strongly relative to reported inflation to generate a meaningful increase in real earnings. This improvement in real purchasing power provides an important fundamental underpinning for the recovery in consumption, consistent with the leg-up in retail sales from the August 2025 lows.

The improvement in domestic demand also helps explain the recent firmness in inflation. Higher input costs—particularly wages and energy—are pushing firms’ cost bases higher, but stronger consumer demand is simultaneously increasing firms’ ability to pass these costs through to final prices. In this sense, the current inflation dynamic is increasingly consistent with a strengthening domestic cycle rather than being driven solely by imported price pressures. Looking ahead, continued wage growth, underpinned by persistent labour shortages, should remain supportive of consumption and encourage the broader characteristics of a maturing business cycle, including higher investment and stronger imports. Key risks remain external geopolitical shocks, particularly those capable of driving oil prices sharply higher while undermining consumer and business confidence, alongside Japan’s already stretched fiscal position.
